C-CURSOR-STATE-HONESTY-1-53C5EC0B.Summary: One `src/` bundle that pays the two staged cursor findings `F309` and `F310`, confined to `src/grace-cursor.ts` and its test. `F310`: after the mandated end-state sequence (terminal, fold, `--assertions final --run-commands`, terminal, fold) `run/` is empty and `gate archive` permits, yet `ngrace cursor show` prints `State: in-progress`. The fold's synthesized covering `opened` is written above the terminal it covers — `writeCoveringOpened` takes its id from `nextEventId` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:782`), `maybeAutoOpenCoveringAllocation` (`:804`) appends it at fold (`:1209`), and the ledger tail on every bundle closed this week is `terminal, command-run, terminal, opened` — while the state derivation reads the last event (`deriveStateFromEvents`, `:465`). The remedy is shape (B): the position's state is derived from the current range's closer, not the last event, so a range that contains a `terminal` (or `discarded`) reads that closer's state even when a synthesized `opened` follows it. `F309`: with the covering allocation `missing` and a hole inside the loose range (a lost event), `cursor recover --fix` writes a covering `opened`, prints `Fix applied: yes`, and on the same diagnosis prints `Fold: blocked (range hole at <id>)`; the fold then refuses. The "yes" is true of the write and false of the repair. The remedy: `--fix` declines to write when the post-write fold would still be blocked by a hole inside the loose range, prints `Fix applied: no` with the hole named, leaves the stream byte-unchanged, and the executor stops and reports the lost event (`D41`). The F308 controls are unchanged: a present covering with a leading hole re-homes; a present covering with a mid-range hole declines; a dense loose range with a missing covering still gets the covering `opened` and folds.

Goals.Goal: **`F310` — a folded stream reads its range's closer.** In `src/grace-cursor.ts`, the shared state projection (`deriveStateFromEvents` at `:465`, and its call sites in `positionProjectionFromBundle` at `:526`, `derivePosition` at `:1422`/`:1537`) becomes range-aware: when the **current range** contains a range-closing event (`terminal` or `discarded`), the position's state is that closer's state; when the range contains no closer, the existing last-event-wins rule is unchanged. The current range is the loose `run/` epoch when any loose event exists, else the last folded ledger epoch; escalation and circuit precedence stay whole-stream and per-task (they are not scoped). A synthesized covering `opened` written above the terminal it covers therefore no longer supersedes that terminal, and the mandated end-state fold reads `complete` in both `ngrace cursor show` and the `run.xml` the fold writes. The synthesized `opened` itself is unchanged: same id (`nextEventId`), same file name, same `max(requirement, openedId + 98)` ceiling.

**`F309` — `recover --fix` refuses to fabricate a covering over a lost event.** In `recoverCursor` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:628`), the shipped skip at `:704` (decline when the covering is `present` and not leading-holed) is joined by the missing-covering case: when `coveringAllocation === "missing"` and the loose range `[from, to]` is **not dense** — an id inside the range is absent from `run/` — no covering `opened` is written. `--fix` returns `fixApplied: false`, the rendered diagnosis reads `Fix applied: no`, the first absent id is named as `range hole at <id>` (`D41`: a lost event no verb may fabricate), and the stream is byte-unchanged; `cursor fold` still exits 1. When the loose range is dense and the covering is missing, `--fix` writes the covering `opened` through the shipped `writeCoveringOpened` exactly as today. A present covering with a leading hole still re-homes; a present covering with a mid-range hole still declines. The executor's next act on the refusal is to stop and report the lost event, never to hand-write a `run/` file.

**The guards — deterministic reds on the base commit, greens after.** Add guards to `src/grace-cursor.test.ts` (no new test file), red on `efae7553e46be6bd8454bf070e43ee458b02c6ab` and green under this bundle's change, on this platform with no Windows dependency: (i) the end-state sequence — seed, open, progress, terminal, fold, `--assertions final --run-commands` (a loose `command-run`), terminal, fold — leaves `run/` empty and `cursor show` must read `complete`, not `in-progress` (red today: the ledger ends `terminal, opened` and `show` reads `in-progress`); (ii) a missing covering with a mid-range hole — `recover --fix`'s rendered output must not say `yes` beside a blocked fold, and must leave the loose `run/` set byte-unchanged (red today: `Fix applied: yes`, `Fold: blocked (range hole at 28 for w0)`, a stray `opened` written); (iii) the F308 controls stay green — a present covering with a leading hole re-homes and folds, a present covering with a mid-range hole declines with `Fix applied: no` and byte-unchanged, and a dense loose range with a missing covering writes and folds. Keep `AC-FORCED-COLLISION`, `AC-UNIQUE-CONCURRENT` and `AC-NO-SILENT-OVERWRITE` green.

**The state-derivation shape, and the shape chosen.** Two shapes were weighed and one chosen. **Shape (B), chosen:** the position's state is derived from the current range's closer rather than the last event. It makes a folded stream read `complete` because the range that contains the fold's synthesized covering `opened` also contains the terminal it covers. **Shape (A), rejected: not producible.** Allocating the synthesized covering `opened` at the first loose id it covers is impossible under the shipped allocator: `nextEventId` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:3494`) returns `max(floor, looseMax + 1, ledgerMax + 1)`, and `writeEventFile` (`:3407`) renumbers a colliding id above the contested one — the behaviour `AC-FORCED-COLLISION` (`src/grace-cursor.test.ts:4106`) pins. The first loose id is always occupied by a real event (a range of one event is that event, the terminal), so an `opened` targeted there lands above the terminal and `F310` recurs; implementing (A) would require writing a colliding id or rewriting a recorded event, both forbidden by `D41`. (A) would also move the id and file name of every fold-synthesized `opened` and the ceiling pins that read `opened.id + 98` (`src/grace-cursor.test.ts:2734`, the `to="102"` pin at `:2822`, `:2891`, `:4342`). **What (B) moves, measured:** the only state change is a current range that contains a closer and a later non-closer. The measured cases are the end-state fold (red today) and a live epoch with a stray terminal (terminal then progress), which today reads `in-progress` while the same stream's `fold` applies (`Fold applied, Events: 4`) because `validateEventsAgainstAllocations` accepts any closer in the range (`:2874`–`:2876`); under (B) it reads `complete`, which is what `fold` already decides, and continuing after a closer requires a new `opened` epoch. Current-range scoping keeps a bounded re-open over a prior epoch's terminal `in-progress` (measured at the base commit: `advance --open-epoch --from 1 --to 99` after a fold reads `in-progress`), which a merged-stream form of (B) would break.

**The `recover --fix` contract, and the ruling it amends.** The shipped skip is `if (pre.coveringAllocation === "present" && !hasLeadingHole(pre)) return { ...pre, fixApplied: false };` (`src/grace-cursor.ts:704`), introduced by `C-RECOVER-FOLDABLE` / `F13` so a healthy open epoch is not re-homed, and extended by `C-EPOCH-OPEN-DEFAULT` / `F308` so a leading hole is re-homed. This bundle amends neither ruling; it extends the missing-covering case with the same principle `F308` stated for the present-covering case: a hole inside the loose range is a genuinely lost event no verb may fabricate. `--fix` writes a covering `opened` only when the loose range is dense; otherwise it declines with `Fix applied: no`, names the first absent id, and leaves the stream byte-unchanged. The `missing` covering diagnosis names the range hole beside `missing valid covering allocation`, so the refusal is not a bare `no`. Multi-worker still refuses before write (`D8.2`); the write remains append-only (`D9`), last-writer-wins per worker (`D9.1`), and terminal-free (`A29.2` / `F12`).
